g-01.enunciado: An insurance company needs to be able to roll back yesterday's faulty load, know who modified a table and when, and have the BI and AI teams query a single source of truth. Which strategy meets all of these requirements?

Parquet files partitioned by date, overwriting the day's partition on each load
CSV files in cloud storage with permissions configured directly on the bucket
Temporary views recreated on every pipeline run from the raw files

g-02.enunciado: You need to incrementally ingest JSON files that arrive continuously in an S3 bucket, processing only the new files on each run. Which option is the most appropriate?

spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "json").load(ruta)
spark.readStream.format("delta").load(ruta)

opciones: They are loaded again and create duplicates in the table

Exporting Salesforce reports to CSV and loading them manually with COPY INTO
A Lakeflow Connect managed connector for Salesforce
Pointing Auto Loader directly at the Salesforce API URL

opciones: INSERT OVERWRITE
MERGE INTO
UPDATE ... FROM
COPY INTO

Repair run

A file arrival trigger

g-10.enunciado: You work in a Databricks Git folder connected to the team's repository. You need to develop a new feature without affecting the main branch that production uses. What do you do?

Create a new branch from the Git folder, then commit and push your changes there

opciones: Manually recreate the jobs in each workspace
Declarative Automation Bundles (formerly Databricks Asset Bundles) with targets and variables
Notebook widgets to type the environment by hand on every run
Different cluster policies per environment

g-12.enunciado: In the Spark UI, the slowest stage of a job shows that almost all tasks finish in under 20 seconds, but one takes 12 minutes. That task's shuffle read is 6 GB, while the median is 300 MB. What is the most likely diagnosis?
opciones: Data skew: a few keys concentrate most of the records
The driver is low on memory
The table has too many small files
The cluster network is saturated

opciones: Partition the table by cliente_id
Enable Liquid Clustering with CLUSTER BY (cliente_id, fecha)
Run ZORDER BY every hour on all columns
Convert the table to CSV format for faster reads

opciones: SELECT on the table only
USE CATALOG on seguros, USE SCHEMA on seguros.silver and SELECT on the table
ALL PRIVILEGES on the seguros catalog
MODIFY on the table and USE SCHEMA on seguros.silver

g-15.enunciado: You run DROP TABLE on an EXTERNAL table registered in Unity Catalog. What happens to the data files?
opciones: They are deleted immediately along with the metadata
They are deleted after 7 days

They are moved to a catalog recycle bin

pla-01.enunciado: You run VACUUM on a Delta table with the default retention. Then you try to time travel to a version from 10 days ago. What most likely happens?
opciones: It works: time travel does not depend on VACUUM
It fails, because VACUUM removed the unreferenced files older than 7 days that this version needed
It works, because VACUUM only deletes the transaction log

pla-02.enunciado: An analyst deleted rows by mistake in a Delta table. Before restoring it, you want to query the table as it was at version 12. Which query do you use?

SELECT * FROM ventas@history(12)
RESTORE ventas SELECT VERSION 12
SELECT * FROM ventas WHERE _version = 12

A fixed-size all-purpose cluster: Databricks shuts it down automatically when it finishes
A single node cluster: your team manages scaling manually

pla-04.enunciado: Many analysts run ad hoc SQL queries and dashboards throughout the day on curated Delta tables. They need good performance with high concurrency, fast startup and controlled cost. Which resource do you recommend?
opciones: A shared single node all-purpose cluster
A serverless SQL warehouse with autoscaling
A job cluster created for each query
A Lakeflow pipeline in continuous mode

opciones: Parquet
Hive
Delta
CSV

opciones: schema.table
metastore.catalog.schema.table
catalog.schema.table
workspace.schema.table

pla-07.enunciado: The security team of a bank in Lima requires that the virtual machines processing customer data run inside the network of its own cloud account, where its firewall rules apply, and that the data stay in its storage. Databricks may keep operating the web UI and the job scheduler. Which option meets these requirements?
opciones: Use serverless compute, because its resources are created inside the network of the customer's cloud account
Move the control plane to the bank's account, because that is where notebook data is processed
Use classic compute: its compute plane runs in the customer's cloud account

pla-08.enunciado: A retail chain runs its nightly PySpark ETL on an all-purpose cluster that stays on all day. It wants to reduce costs and isolate each run, but the process needs an init script that installs the corporate monitoring agent on every node. Which option meets these requirements?

Use a classic jobs cluster with the init script, created per run and terminated when it finishes
Run the job on serverless compute for jobs and register the init script in the environment configuration
Run the PySpark notebook on a classic SQL warehouse with the init script configured

pla-09.enunciado: A data scientist at an insurance company needs an all-purpose cluster just for herself. Her legacy code uses the RDD API, requires Databricks Runtime for Machine Learning and must read Unity Catalog tables. Which compute configuration meets these requirements?
opciones: An all-purpose cluster in standard access mode, shared with the rest of the team
Serverless compute for notebooks, to avoid managing infrastructure
A cluster in No isolation shared mode, which applies no language restrictions
An all-purpose cluster in dedicated access mode assigned to her

pla-10.enunciado: The finance team of a telecom reviews the monthly bill for its pro SQL warehouse and notices two charges: one from Databricks and another from the cloud provider. opciones: With serverless, the DBU rate already includes the compute; you do not pay separately for the virtual machines
With serverless you still pay the cloud provider separately for the virtual machines, but there is no DBU charge
With serverless you only pay a fixed monthly fee, regardless of how long the warehouse is active
Pro and serverless have the same model; the only difference is startup time

pla-11.enunciado: At a fintech, a job rewrites the Delta table `riesgo.scores_clientes` every hour while a dashboard queries it. The BI team requires that the dashboard never see half-written data: it must see either the complete previous version or the complete new one. Which mechanism meets this requirement?
opciones: Unity Catalog locks the table for reads while the job's write lasts
Parquet files are written atomically, so the file format is enough
The Delta Lake transaction log, which only exposes committed versions
The Photon engine retries the dashboard query until the write finishes

pla-12.enunciado: A retail company has three workspaces (dev, qa and prod) in the same cloud region. It wants to define permissions only once, have centralized lineage and auditing, and use the same catalogs from all three workspaces. Which option meets these requirements?
opciones: Keep each workspace's Hive metastore and replicate the GRANTs with a script in each one
Create one Unity Catalog metastore for the region and assign it to the three workspaces
Create a separate Unity Catalog metastore per workspace and sync permissions between them
Enable table access control on each workspace's clusters separately

pla-13.enunciado: An insurance company appends new policies to the Delta table `polizas` every night. Today, the source DataFrame brings an extra column, `canal_venta`, that does not exist in the table, and the code does not use any schema evolution option. What happens when the write runs?
opciones: The write completes and the `canal_venta` column is added to the table automatically
The write completes, but the `canal_venta` values are silently discarded
The table is overwritten with the new schema and the previous policies are lost
The write fails due to schema enforcement and the table remains unchanged

pla-14.enunciado: A bank has 40 small jobs triggered by file arrival throughout the day. Each one processes in about 3 minutes, but today it waits several more minutes for its jobs cluster to start. They want to reduce that wait without managing instance types or paying for idle machines. Which option meets these requirements?
opciones: Run the jobs on serverless compute for jobs, which starts quickly and is billed only for usage
Create an instance pool with several idle instances always available for the jobs clusters
Use a single always-on all-purpose cluster shared by the 40 jobs
Schedule the jobs with a cron every 5 minutes instead of the file arrival trigger

ing-01.enunciado: When configuring Auto Loader with schema inference, what is the `cloudFiles.schemaLocation` option for?

It replaces the stream's checkpoint location

Define how often a micro-batch runs
Store the records rejected by quality checks

trigger(continuous="1 second")
trigger(availableNow=True)

ing-04.enunciado: With Auto Loader and the default schema evolution mode (addNewColumns), a file arrives with a new column. What happens?
opciones: The new column is silently ignored
The stream stops, updates the stored schema and, when restarted, includes the new column
The column's data goes to _rescued_data and the schema never changes
A new table with the additional column is created automatically

ing-05.enunciado: Your bronze table has a schema agreed with the business that must not change, but you also do not want the stream to stop or to lose data if a file brings unexpected columns. Which Auto Loader schema evolution mode do you use?
opciones: addNewColumns
failOnNewColumns
rescue
none, without a rescued data column

ing-06.enunciado: Auto Loader ingests from a directory that already holds millions of files, and listing the folder on each run has become slow and expensive. Which change reduces that cost?

Run directory listing more frequently
Replace Auto Loader with spark.read.json on the whole folder
Reduce cloudFiles.maxFilesPerTrigger to 1

opciones: cloudFiles.schemaHints = "monto DECIMAL(12,2)"
cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes = false
mergeSchema = true on the write
Rename the column in the source file

ing-08.enunciado: A vendor's new files bring an additional column, and your COPY INTO into a Delta table fails because of a schema mismatch. How do you allow the column to be added to the table?
opciones: COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema' = 'true')
COPY_OPTIONS ('force' = 'true')
Run VACUUM before COPY INTO
Change FILEFORMAT to TEXT

opciones: COPY INTO scheduled every 5 minutes
Auto Loader
spark.read on the whole folder with mode('overwrite')
Upload the files manually from the UI

A Lakeflow Connect managed connector for SQL Server
COPY INTO with a JDBC connection string
A daily CSV export and manual load

Delta Sharing with the provider

failOnNewColumns

ing-39.enunciado: A bank consumes the paginated REST API of a credit bureau, which requires a token.
